newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Evans says wages high for inflation regime.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Evans says wages high for inflation regime.

text.p: Australian Treasury Secretary Ted Evans said on Thursday he saw wages growth steady at about one percent a quarter, including the March quarter, but that average weekly earnings were still high for the current low inflation regime.
But Evans also said he agreed that this week's wages data was not inconsistent with inflation forecasts.

When asked if he would agree that there was nothing in Wednesday's or Thursday's wages data that was inconsistent with forecasts of inflation of about two percent over the next 18 months or so, he said: "Yes, I'd agree with that."
Evans described recent average weekly wages data showing a sharp acceleration in private wages as not believeable.

"The best one could draw out of those figures is that we've been running at one percent a quarter for some time, including going back through to that low March quarter of last year so it's doubtful that's there's been an acceleration as such," Evans told an Australian Business Economists luncheon.
"Nonetheless it is a high average wage outcome for ordinary time earnings to be living with, if one is looking at an inflation target of two to three percent," Evans said.
He had been asked what he thought of this week's wages data.

Evans said the wages data would be just one part of any policy decisions and that any thought that wages concerns dominated Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane's considerations on interest rates was exaggerated.

"People may have drawn a rather long bow from the government of its conern where aggregate wages are going to be suggesting that one single indicator would affect his or anyone else's decisions on these matters," he said.
Evans said the unreliabilty of the data emphasised that teh figures should not be relied on solely.

Earlier the Australian Bureau of Statistics released data showing private sector wages rose 1.3 percent in the three months to February 28, up from 0.8 percent and 0.5 percent respectively in the previous two quarters.
All sector wages rose 1.0 percent for the quarter, revised down from a preliminary measure of 1.3 percent, and rose 4.3 percent for the year.
Public sector wages rose 0.7 percent for the quarter and was 7.1 percent higher for the year.
Evans said neither the public sector nor the public sector data released before Thursday morning was unbelievable.
"We're stuck with compositional problems there," he said.

The Reserve Bank of Australia warned earlier this month that aggregate wages growth was uncomfortably high and if it accelerated further the central bank would have no choice but to raise rates to prevent higher inflation.
Economists believe the RBA is uncomfortable when wages growth gets into the 4.5 percent to 5.0 percent band.
The government has also said wages growth was high.
